'''Gopal Chandra Kundu''' (born 2 November 1959<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |date=2005-01-30 |title=Molecular Mechanisms behind Melanoma and Breast Cancers: Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize-winner. R Gopal C. Kundu's works |url=https://niscpr.res.in/includes/images/csirnews/csirnews_30jan05.pdf |journal=CSIR News |volume=55 |issue=2 |pages=20–21}}</ref>) is an Indian cell and cancer biologist who worked as a scientist at the Indian [[National Centre for Cell Science]].<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=167 | title=Brief Profile of the Awardee | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=5 October 2016}}</ref> He is known for his contributions towards the understanding the mechanism of cancer progression in [[Breast cancer|breast]], [[melanoma]] and other cancers and development of novel therapeutic targets and target-based therapy in cancers.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=1999 | access-date=5 October 2016 | pages=34 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304043957/http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | archive-date=4 March 2016 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

An elected fellow of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="Fellow profile - G C Kundu">{{cite web | url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Kundu,_Dr_Gopal_Chandra | title=Fellow profile - G C Kundu | publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences | date=2016 | access-date=6 October 2016}}</ref> and the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]],<ref name="NASI fellows">{{cite web|url=http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=K |title=NASI fellows |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |date=2016 |access-date=20 October 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160315081652/http://nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=K |archive-date=15 March 2016 }}</ref> he received the [[National Bioscience Award for Career Development]] of the [[Department of Biotechnology]] in 2003.<ref name="N-BIOS Prize">{{cite web | url=http://dbtindia.nic.in/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/list_of_bioscience_awardees.pdf | title=N-BIOS Prize | publisher=Department of Biotechnology | date=2016 | access-date=20 October 2016 | archive-date=4 March 2018 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180304191331/http://dbtindia.nic.in/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/list_of_bioscience_awardees.pdf | url-status=dead }}</ref> He was awarded the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], the highest Indian science awards, in 2004.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=201 | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=5 October 2016}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Kundu studied chemistry and biology at the [[Scottish Church College]] in Calcutta (now [[Kolkata]]), India. He obtained a B.Sc. with major in chemistry from the [[University of Calcutta]] (affiliating university of SCC) in 1980. He completed M.Sc. in chemistry at the University of Calcutta in 1982.<ref name=":0" /> He entered the [[Bose Institute]], Kolkata, for a doctoral course and earned his Ph.D. in 1989 in [[protein]] [[biochemistry]] In 1989, he went to [[Cleveland Clinic Foundation]], USA, as a post-doctoral fellow. For the next eight years, he worked as a research associate at the [[University of Colorado]] (1990-1992), and then as a senior research associate at the [[University of Wyoming]] (1992-1993) and the [[National Institutes of Health]], Bethesda (1993-1998). He became specialised in [[cardiovascular]] biology, [[inflammation]] and [[Immunotherapy|immunomodulation]] during that period. In 1998, he joined the [[National Centre for Cell Science]] (NCCS), [[Pune]], as Scientist-D.<ref>{{cite web| title =Dr. Gopal Kundu| publisher =[[National Centre For Cell Science|NCCS]]| date =1 January 2001| url =http://www.nccs.res.in/gck.html| access-date =8 November 2011| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20110927054319/http://www.nccs.res.in/gck.html| archive-date =27 September 2011| url-status =dead}}</ref> At NCCS, he published his most important research papers covering [[tumor]] biology, regulation of gene expression, cell signaling, [[angiogenesis]], cancer [[therapeutics]], [[biomarker]] studies for cancer detection, and [[nanomedicine]].<ref>{{cite web| title =DBT neurobiology task force| publisher = [[Neurobiology]]| date =5 March 2004| url =http://dbt-neuro.ncbs.res.in/node/74}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title =Curriculum vitae| publisher =[[apoptosis]]| date =20 August 2005| url =http://www.apoptosis2005.org/profiles/gopal_kundu.htm| access-date =9 November 2011| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20120425152323/http://www.apoptosis2005.org/profiles/gopal_kundu.htm| archive-date =25 April 2012| url-status =dead}}</ref>

In 2019, Kundu retired from the government service at superannuation age. He was immediately appointed as director of research and development at the [[Kalinga Institute of Industrial Technology]] (KIIT), a private university in Bhubaneswar, Odissa. He also holds professor positions in biotechnology at KIIT and in medicine and molecular research at Kalinga Institute of Medical Science.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2023 |title=Gopal C. Kundu |url=https://biotech.kiit.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/GopalCKundu-KSBT.pdf |access-date=2025-02-21 |website=KIIT School of Biotechnology |language=en-US}}</ref>

He serves as Editorial Board Member of ''[[Current Molecular Medicine]]'', ''Current Chemical Biology'', ''[[Frontiers in Medicine]]'', ''[[International Journal of Oncology]]'', ''Molecular Medicine Reports'', ''The Open Cancer Journal'' and ''[[American Journal of Cancer Research]]''. He is an associate editor of ''[[Molecular Cancer]]'' and ''Journal of Cancer Metastasis and Treatment.<ref name=":1" />''

== Awards and honours ==
Kundu is elected Fellow of [[the National Academy of Sciences, India]] (2003), the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] (2006) and [[Indian National Science Academy]] (2023). He is member of [[American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology]] and [[New York Academy of Sciences]]. He was elected Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] in 2023.<ref name=":1" />

In 2013, he received the 7th National Grassroots Innovation Awards from the National Innovation Foundation for his works in cancer biology.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2013-03-13 |title=Pune based National Centre for Cell Science gets award |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/pune/pune-based-national-centre-for-cell-science-gets-award/articleshow/18952990.cms |access-date=2025-02-21 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

==Controversy==
A controversy erupted in the NCCS in 2006 when an anonymous mail alleged that Kundu and others might have misrepresented data in a paper published in the ''[[Journal of Biological Chemistry]]''. The allegation was that they had rehashed the same set of data which they had published earlier.<ref>{{cite web| title =Kundu-JBC Case| publisher = [[Society for Scientific Values]]| url =http://www.scientificvalues.org/kundu_case.html}}</ref> An internal committee of the NCCS advised the authors to take back their paper, however an independent committee led by [[G. Padmanabhan]], a former director of Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore, concluded that there was no manipulation in the data.<ref>{{cite news| title =Indicted there, acquitted here| work = [[The Telegraph (Kolkata)|The Telegraph]]| date =6 March 2007| author= G.S. mudur| url =http://www.telegraphindia.com/1070306/asp/frontpage/story_7476120.asp| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20110525194534/http://www.telegraphindia.com/1070306/asp/frontpage/story_7476120.asp| url-status =dead| archive-date =25 May 2011| location=Calcutta, India}}</ref> On 23 February 2007, the ''Journal of Biological Chemistry'' withdrew the paper amid allegations of data manipulation, although the authors maintained that the two papers used different set of data though similar experiments.
